implementation_summary: Correction for CHK-BE-503-UNIT (EV-0081). BE-709 registered a Hindi label table, so the test 'a language without its own table falls back to English wording' no longer covered a language without a table when it used 'hi'. It now uses 'te', which still has no label table. Both assertions are unchanged: doc.language is 'en' and the title is en.documentTitles.findings. Test-only change.
tests_proposed: When per-file 'hi' wording tables or a full-English fallback are added: a test that a 'hi' Structure/Content/Findings document has no mixed-language fixed wording
risks: Hindi documents mix languages: labelsFor('hi') returns BE-709's Hindi DocumentLabels and the document is marked language 'hi', but the per-file wording tables in structure.ts:77, content.ts:121 and findings.ts:48 cover only en and ta, so structureWording/contentWording/findingsWording('hi') fall back to English. Result: Hindi labels and titles with English Section kinds, missing-alt note, call-to-action and form wording, group/impact/effort wording, skipped-page wording and the 'Website' line. No test covers this today.
handoff: Test-only change. Fix for the Hindi mix in a later task: add 'hi' tables to the WORDING maps in structure.ts, content.ts and findings.ts, or make the builders use English labels too when a file has no table for the language. Adding a label table for 'te' later will break this test again; switch it to another language that has no table.
